subject: Data lifecycle exception & SIG evidence — CareBridge follow-up
messages:
From: CareBridge Security <security@carebridge.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: m.singh@carebridge.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Data lifecycle exception & SIG evidence — follow up

Hi Sean / Irene,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. We ran the SIG v4 and CAIQ checklist against a few things and CareBridge has two items that need clarification before we can close the security review:

1) Tenant-scoped ephemeral session traces: our compliance requirement is that session-level debug traces for sensitive flows be retained no longer than 30 days unless explicitly requested for a legal hold. We need to understand whether Redwood can enforce a per-tenant TTL that overrides the default platform retention, and what the exception process looks like.

2) Proof of deletion and sampling: for SOC 2 evidence we need a sample workflow and artifacts that demonstrate full deletion (and not just redaction). Specifically: sample audit trail entries (who/when), a deletion job run log, and a redacted sample of session logs.

I've attached our SIG questions spreadsheet with the rows we've flagged (carebridge_sig_questions_v4.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Support a tenant-specific TTL configuration for session traces?
- Produce a one-off proof-of-delete package for the tenant (including DB-level deletion manifests or S3 object manifests)?

We're aiming to finish the review by Friday (Nov 6). Can you let us know what you can provide and an ETA?

Thanks,
Maya Singh
DPO, CareBridge Health
security@carebridge.com

Attachment: carebridge_sig_questions_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet, 43KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: CareBridge Security <security@carebridge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle exception & SIG evidence — follow up

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, we can support tenant-specific TTLs for session traces; yes, we can produce a proof-of-delete package for a scoped period. Below is a quick plan and next steps.

Summary / Plan
- Tenant TTLs: Redwood Private and Dedicated customers can set per-tenant TTLs for ephemeral session traces via the deployment config. For Hosted customers we support tenant-scoped retention via a per-tenant metadata flag + background eviction job. We will need an SLO and a signed exception form for permanent changes.

- Proof-of-delete package: we can generate an evidence bundle that includes: deletion job logs, S3 object deletion manifests (or DB deletion manifests depending on the storage backend), SHA256 hashes of deleted objects for auditability, and a brief attestation signed by our Security Ops.

What I need from you
1) Confirm the tenant ID (the account you want us to target).
2) Confirm whether you want TTL enforced immediately or via a time-gated change (e.g., after your legal hold window closes).
3) Any PII masking rules we should apply to the sample logs (we can provide redacted CSVs).

ETA and attachments
- I'll have the retention matrix and an initial mapping to SIG v4 rows by EOD Nov 4. Irene will follow with the proof-of-delete template and a sample redacted log by Nov 4–5.

Attaching a short retention matrix to show our defaults and where tenant overrides plug in.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

+1 415 555 0132

From: Maya Singh <m.singh@carebridge.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, security@carebridge.com
Date: 2026-11-04T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle exception & SIG evidence — follow up

Hi Sean — thanks, that helps. CAREBRIDGE-ACCT-9984 is the tenant ID to scope. We'd like the TTL to be reduced to 30 days for session traces related to clinical workflows (these are labeled with metadata.topic=clinical in our events). Two clarifications:

- Is the per-tenant TTL enforced immediately or is there a FIFO backlog before the eviction job runs? We need to know if any data older than 30 days will remain for more than 48 hours after the change.
- For the proof-of-delete: we require an audit trail formatted for ingestion into our governance tool (CSV with columns: object_key, deleted_at, deleted_by, deletion_job_id). Can you confirm you can produce that schema?

Also, because this will be a permanent deviation from your standard retention for this tenant, our legal team will want a short written exception form that we can reference in our contract addendum. Please include the change window and the responsible SRE contact.

Thanks,
Maya

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: m.singh@carebridge.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-04T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle exception & SIG evidence — follow up

Maya — thanks for the tenant ID and questions. Below is a consolidated response and the next steps; I've attached a short sample CSV (sample-redacted-session-logs.csv) and a deletion-manifest template.

1) Enforcement latency
- Hosted mode (CareBridge account): when we flip a tenant TTL the background eviction job runs in waves; typical propagation is under 2 hours, with a rare tail up to 24 hours for very large backfills. For your request (30-day TTL), we can run a targeted backfill job for the tenant to purge any trace older than 30 days; that job would complete within 24–48 hours depending on data volume. If you need guaranteed sub-48-hour enforcement we will schedule the targeted backfill as part of the change.

2) Proof-of-delete schema
- We can emit a CSV matching your governance schema with columns: object_key, deleted_at (ISO8601), deleted_by (svc-account or user email), deletion_job_id. The manifest will also include storage_backend and checksum (SHA256). See attached "deletion-manifest-template.csv" in the bundle.

3) Auditable evidence and attestation
- Evidence bundle will include: deletion-manifest.csv, deletion-job-log.txt, sample-redacted-session-logs.csv (PII redacted per agreed rules), and a short attestation letter signed by our Security Ops and Head of SRE. We can also include the SIG v4 row mapping for your review.

4) Exception form / contract language
- We will produce a one-page exception statement including: tenant_id, effective_date, TTL value, scope (metadata.topic=clinical), responsible SRE contact (Asha Reddy, asha.reddy@redwood.ai), and rollback conditions. We will provide that to your legal team as a PDF and are happy to walk the clause into your addendum.

Next steps / ETA
- Today (Nov 4): I am attaching a sample redacted log and the deletion-manifest template for schema validation.
- Nov 5 (EOD): We will deliver the full deletion-job log and the initial deletion-manifest for verification.
- Nov 6: Attestation letter and exception form for signature.

If the schema looks good, we can proceed with the backfill on Nov 5. Please reply with a quick confirmation and any additional masking rules.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
